reasoning_summary: The deterministic verdict is INCONCLUSIVE with no failed checks. All five uncertainty components (averaging, statistics, mesh, time, domain) are unmeasured for both quantities, so ACCEPT is not allowed. There is no FAIL to justify REJECT.
R0's physics_regime check is INCONCLUSIVE. The lift amplitude changes by +25.8% across the analysed window, so the wake is not yet a sustained limit cycle (decaying or still growing).

The stationary window for R0 starts at 15.276 convective units, which is flagged as the MSER cap. The window holds only 3 cycles (<4), and the record ends at 39.99 convective units. The shedding period is about 622.74 steps at 0.01 convective units per step, i.e. about 6.2 convective units.

R0 reports a mean Cd of 1.2961 over the submitted averaging window and 1.3039 over the stationary window. The Cd drift is 4.01% and the Cd 95% CI is 0.044509. The reported St is 0.16129, the stationary-window St is 0.16058, and the FFT St is 0.16169. The St frequency resolution is 0.033333 (about 21% of St), and the St statistical uncertainty is 3.58%. Both figures exceed or are close to the 3% tolerance.
Because the transient has not finished, any mesh, time-step or domain comparison made now would mix discretisation effects with unsteady drift. A longer R0 record must come first.

The other recorded checks pass, so there is no evidence of a setup defect: mesh OK, max Courant 0.73373, mass imbalance 8.3333e-11, Re matches the spec, force references are consistent, and the scheme is second order.

RUN_LONGER on R0 is also the cheapest useful step (979 s estimated). It leaves budget for later mesh, domain and time-step experiments within the 12x-root compute cap of about 4700 s. The default 100 D/U adds roughly 16 shedding cycles.

hypotheses.hypothesis: R0's lift amplitude is still growing or decaying at t=40 D/U, so the 15.3 D/U window start still includes transient. This explains the +25.8% amplitude change, the 4.01% Cd drift and the 3-cycle window.
hypotheses.test: Continue R0 by 100 D/U. Confirm that the lift amplitude settles to within a few percent across successive windows, that the Cd drift falls well below the 3% tolerance, and that the stationary window then holds 4 or more cycles with a St frequency resolution much finer than 0.033.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Once stationary, the mean Cd and St of R0 differ from the current values by more than 3%. The 3-cycle and drifting window is biased, and the current Cd (1.2961 vs 1.3039) and St (0.16129 vs 0.16058) spread is only a lower bound on the true uncertainty.
hypotheses.test: Compare Cd and St from the extended stationary window with the R0 values. A change >3% (beyond noise) confirms the hypothesis, and a change well under 3% refutes it.

next_experiment.reason: The physics_regime check shows the lift amplitude still changing by 25.8%. The stationary window has only 3 cycles, and its start sits at the MSER cap. Averaging and statistics are blocking checks for both quantities, and mesh, time and domain comparisons are only meaningful on a stationary limit cycle. It is also the cheapest experiment (979 s estimated).
next_experiment.expected_outcome: The lift amplitude saturates and a stationary window of about 10 or more cycles emerges. The Cd CI and drift and the St statistical uncertainty then fall below 0.5*tolerance (1.5%). The averaging and statistics components become measurable, so mesh, domain and time-step experiments can follow on a valid baseline.

reasoning_summary: The deterministic verdict is INCONCLUSIVE with no failed checks. ACCEPT is not allowed because mesh, time and domain are unmeasured for both quantities. REJECT is not allowed because there is no FAIL.

R1 (RUN_LONGER from R0) settled the averaging and statistics components. R1 has 12 stationary cycles. Its Cd CI95 is 3.4541e-05, its Cd drift is 0.0001195, and its St frequency resolution is 0.0076923. Statistics PASS for both quantities.

R1's stationary-window values are Cd 1.3311, St 0.16343 (FFT 0.16343) and rms Cl 0.22857. R0's reported values were Cd 1.2961 and St 0.16129. R0 was therefore biased by 2.631% in Cd and 1.312% in St. That was the transient-contaminated 3-cycle window.

The averaging bias is added linearly to the error budget. For Cd, 2.631% of the 3% tolerance is already used, so very little room is left for the mesh, time and domain components. Cd acceptance looks hard for R0 as submitted. Mesh, time and domain are still unmeasured, and no FAIL has been demonstrated, so REJECT is not justified yet.

The physics_regime check is INCONCLUSIVE only because of R0's 25.8% lift-amplitude change across its short window. R1's 12-cycle record has a stable Cd drift of 0.0001195, which is consistent with the transient having ended.

The mesh is the most likely source of a change larger than 3%. The representative cell size is 0.45745 D, with 160 cells around the cylinder and 111 streamwise wake cells. The wake's last cell is 1.0209 D and the wall first cell is 0.005 D. Cd and St are both sensitive to near-wake resolution.

The domain has 30 D upstream, 50 D downstream and 40 D half-height, with a blockage ratio of 0.0125 and a symmetry lateral boundary. It is already fairly large, so domain error is less likely to be the dominant term.

Budget: 2.5 of 12.0 root-compute units are used, which leaves roughly 3700 s. The menu costs are 1812 s for REFINE_MESH, 1567 s for REDUCE_TIME_STEP and 1040 s for EXPAND_DOMAIN. All three together would not fit, so the most informative one goes first. Courant 0.73373 with second-order backward time stepping makes time error plausibly smaller than mesh error.
Parent R1 is chosen because its 12-cycle stationary window gives a clean baseline for comparing Cd and St. R0's 3-cycle window would mix mesh effects with transient noise.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The mesh (cell size 0.45745 D, wake last cell 1.0209 D) is too coarse in the near wake. Refinement will shift the stationary Cd (1.3311) or St (0.16343) by more than the 3% tolerance, or by more than 1.5% (0.5*tolerance).
hypotheses.test: Run REFINE_MESH with factor 1.4142 from R1. Compare the stationary-window Cd and St with R1's values. A change above 3% (beyond 2x noise) is a FAIL that confirms the hypothesis. A change well below 1.5% refutes it.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Time and domain errors are small. Courant 0.73373 with second-order backward stepping and a 1.25% blockage ratio should give changes well below 1.5%.
hypotheses.test: Run REDUCE_TIME_STEP and EXPAND_DOMAIN afterwards, as far as the budget allows. Compare the stationary Cd and St with R1's.

next_experiment.reason: Mesh resolution is the largest unmeasured uncertainty component. The representative cell size is 0.45745 D and the wake last cell is 1.0209 D. R1 provides a stationary 12-cycle baseline. The Cd averaging bias of R0 (2.631%) already takes most of the 3% budget, so a mesh error of even a few tenths of a percent matters.
next_experiment.expected_outcome: If the stationary Cd and St change by less than about 1.5% relative to R1 (Cd 1.3311, St 0.16343), the mesh component passes and the remaining budget can go to the time-step or domain run. A change above 3% (beyond noise) would be a deterministic FAIL, which would justify REJECT.
